questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Scalar Projection Using Angles and Magnitudes
questions.problem: Suppose $|\,c\,|=10$ and the angle between vectors $c$ and $d$ is $\theta =\frac{\pi }{3}.$ Find the scalar projection of $c$ onto $d.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{d}\,c & =|\,c\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =10\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =10\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Scalar Projection Using Components
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 6+(-1)\cdot 2+2\cdot (-3)}{\sqrt{{6}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-3)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{4}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{a}\,b & =\frac{b\cdot a}{|\,a\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}+{a}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{9}} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a-{\text{comp}}_{a}\,b & =\frac{4}{7}-\frac{4}{3} \\  & =4(\frac{1}{7}-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =4(\frac{3}{21}-\frac{7}{21}) \\  & =-\frac{16}{21}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Projecting a Vector Onto a Perpendicular Vector
questions.problem: Let $p=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$ and $q=[\begin{aligned}15 \\ \sqrt{2} \\ x\end{aligned}].$ Given that the scalar projection of $p$ onto $q$ is $0,$ find the value of $x.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $p$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $q$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
p⊥q\,⟹\,p\cdot q=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & ={p}_{x}\cdot {q}_{x}+{p}_{y}\cdot {q}_{y}+{p}_{z}\cdot {q}_{z} \\  & =(-2)\cdot 15+0\cdot \sqrt{2}+5\cdot x \\  & =5x-30.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & =0 \\ 5x-30 & =0 \\ 5x & =30 \\ x & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $p=i+2j+xk$ and $q=3i+6j-3k.$ Given that the scalar projection of $p$ onto $q$ is zero, find the value of $x.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $p$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $q$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
p⊥q\,⟹\,p\cdot q=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & ={p}_{x}\cdot {q}_{x}+{p}_{y}\cdot {q}_{y}+{p}_{z}\cdot {q}_{z} \\  & =1\cdot 3+2\cdot 6+x\cdot (-3) \\  & =15-3x.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & =0 \\ 15-3x & =0 \\ 3x & =15 \\ x & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z} \\  & =4\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 0+3\cdot x \\  & =3x+8.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+8 & =0 \\ 3x & =-8 \\ x & =-\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Suppose $|\,\mathbf{a}\,|=13$ and the angle between vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ is $\theta = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}.$ Find the scalar projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =|\,a\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =13\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}) \\  & =13\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{13}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Let $\mathbf{a}=\langle 3,3,-1 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{b}=\langle 2,-7,0 \rangle.$ Find the scalar projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$

$$
